novelty_flags.label: thm:one-scm-sharpness
novelty_flags.one_line: This is a graph-and-query instantiation of Duarte et al.'s general exact response-function polynomial reduction, not an independently new identification kernel.

novelty_flags.label: thm:npm-cert-termination / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The core says Duarte et al.'s Algorithm 2 supplies anytime outer bounds, but Algorithm 2 formulates the polynomial program; the anytime dual branch-and-bound procedure is Algorithm 3.

novelty_flags.label: thm:positive-rank-two-contraction
novelty_flags.one_line: The failed in-catalogue scm_prox_recant_pid_v1 already poses the same positive-cell failed-completeness recanting endpoint-exclusion/contraction kernel.

soundness_flags.label: def:response-fiber; thm:one-scm-sharpness; thm:npm-cert-termination
soundness_flags.one_line: The response-code districts omit the root treatment A, so p_o(v) has no declared response distribution generating the A coordinate of an observed cell; add an A district/mass or formulate the fiber conditional on A with declared arm probabilities.

soundness_flags.label: oeq:singular-modulus-frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: “target-restricted Robinson metric regularity of the endpoint fibers” is neither defined nor tied to the declared Rob(P) predicate, so the requested equivalence has no fixed mathematical RHS.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:robinson-root-n
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Robinson regularity is assumed as a sufficient local regime, not derived for generic feasible laws.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Root-n excess enlargement is claimed only conditional on Rob(P); no necessity or generic root-n assertion is retained.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1784-1785, Algorithm 2 discussion and Theorem 1; pp. 1787-1789, Algorithm 3 discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Algorithm 2 produces a polynomial program whose optimization gives sharp causal bounds by Theorem 1; the anytime dual-envelope and epsilon-sharp optimization procedure is Algorithm 3, not Algorithm 2.
The paper defines proxies for the hidden recanting witness, imposes completeness of Z or W plus bridge assumptions, and identifies E[Y(M2(M1(0),1),M1(0),0)] through three bridge-based formulas.
The paper develops proxy partial identification without completeness or identified bridge functions, including related settings with hidden mediators.
The paper develops exact p-value inversion and confidence intervals for real-valued functions of multinomial parameters with finite-sample type-I-error control.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair the response-function model by explicitly coding the root-treatment district and then restate every observed-cell polynomial and reconstruction claim against that complete SCM code.

Replace the response-fiber representation and the rank-two contraction theorem as headline contributions with a result not already posed in scm_prox_recant_pid_v1, such as a proved generic-class strict-contraction criterion or a computable target-specific regularity frontier.

Define a precise target-restricted metric-regularity predicate and state an observable/certifiable condition whose satisfaction yields the modulus exponent; retain the singular statement as an OEQ only after that focal object is fixed.

recommended_next_step: Continue revision: first make the SCM response code and singular-regularity target well-defined, then pivot the duplicate contraction kernel toward a genuinely distinct field-level frontier.
